source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-24

procedures.title: Rear stabilizer shaft: replace
steps: Raise the rear and support it at the frame side rails on stands.
Disconnect the stabilizer shaft from both torque arms (see figure 64 in the manual); remove its brackets from the frame and take the shaft out.
Check the bushings for deterioration and the shaft for bends, breaks or other faults; replace parts as needed and do not try to straighten the shaft.
Fit the bushings on the shaft and loosely attach the shaft to the torque arms and frame brackets.
Position the shaft so it sits correctly once tightened, then torque the attaching bolts to specification.

procedures.title: Corvette rear axle: general description
notes: The carrier housing holds the differential and hypoid gears and sits on a crossmember mounted to the frame; it drives the wheels through U-joints and drive shafts (see figure 66 in the manual).
The overhung pinion runs on two preloaded tapered roller bearings; the two-pinion differential runs on tapered roller bearings.
Pinion depth (mounting distance), differential bearing preload and backlash are all set with shims.
The side gears drive two splined yokes held sideways by snap rings on the splined end; the yokes run in caged needle bearings pressed into the carrier...
